item.title: Bolsa de Rosario recorta estimación de cosecha soja Argentina, sube previsión maíz
item.description: La Bolsa de Comercio de Rosario (BCR) recortó el miércoles su estimación de cosecha para la soja 2026/27 de Argentina a 47,8 millones de toneladas, mientras que subió su previsión para la producción 26/27 de maíz a entre 67,5 y 70,5 millones de toneladas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La Bolsa de Comercio de Rosario (BCR) recortó el miércoles su estimación de cosecha para la soja 2026/27 de Argentina a 47,8 millones de toneladas, mientras que subió su previsión para la producción 26/27 de maíz a entre 67,5 y 70,5 millones de toneladas. El mes pasado la BCR había estimado la producción de soja en 48 millones de toneladas y la de maíz en 66 millones de toneladas. En el caso del trigo 2026/27, la Bolsa de Rosario subió su estimación de cosecha del cereal en 500.000 toneladas, a 21 millones de toneladas.

item.title: Trading Day: $100 oil bites
item.description: Stocks around the world fell on Wednesday as entrenched conflict in the Middle East pushed oil prices above $100 a barrel, while bond yields rose to fresh multi-year highs as investors reacted negatively to the U.S. Treasury's plan to triple bond buybacks.
item.dc:creator: Jamie McGeever
item.content:encoded: [USN:L4N4510P8 TEXT:"Stocks"] around the world fell on Wednesday as [USN:L6N45118W TEXT:"entrenched conflict"] in the Middle East pushed oil prices above [USN:P8N43I0BY TEXT:"$100 a barrel"], while bond yields rose to fresh multi-year highs as investors reacted negatively to the U.S. Treasury's plan to triple [USN:L1N4510P7 TEXT:"bond buybacks"]. In [USN:L6N4500TK TEXT:"my column today"], I look at what might replace the Japanese yen as the funding currency of choice in global FX carry trades. Swissie? Loonie? Euro? There's no obvious candidate. Today's Key Reads Iran said on Wednesday it had attacked 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz after the U.S. sank five Iranian oil tankers, in the [USN:L6N451042 TEXT:"biggest declared wave of tit-for-tat attacks on shipping"] by both sides since the start of the six-month-old war. EXCLUSIVE - AI agents unleashed by OpenAI used more than 10 previously undisclosed websites for unsanctioned communications earlier this year, according to six sets of independent investigators and data reviewed by Reuters, showing that [USN:L6N4510WC TEXT:"the agents’ rogue activity"] was wider ranging than previously disclosed. The United States has banned a broad swath of Canadian alcoholic beverages, motorcycles and dairy products from import, [USN:L6N44W10Z TEXT:"sharply escalating an already acrimonious trade spat."] Even two wars and sky-high energy prices haven't cooled the world economy. Global growth is running hot into the second half of the year, forcing asset managers to find firebreaks while staying invested. Higher interest rates may be the only policy brake left, observes ROI's Mike Dolan . How much oil is flowing through the [USN:L1N44Y067 TEXT:"Strait of Hormuz"]? Traders, energy executives and government officials are all trying to [USN:L1N44A048 TEXT:"figure it out"] — but are reaching wildly different conclusions. It is, however, increasingly clear that this mystery has introduced a residual risk premium into crude prices that could remain deeply entrenched for months. [USN:L6N4500W5 TEXT:"Analysis from ROI's Ron Bousso."] Today's Key Market Moves STOCKS: South Korea outperforms in Asia, +1.3%. [USN:L4N4510FH TEXT:"Europe"] -1.4% to 1-month low. Big three U.S. indices all lower: S&P 500 -0.5%, Nasdaq -0.6%, Dow -0.8%. SECTORS/SHARES: Every sector on the S&P 500 falls, except energy (+1). Industrials -1.5%, utilities -1.2%. [USN:L6N4500XV TEXT:"Meta"] +6.6%, [USN:L6N4510Z3 TEXT:"Apple"] -0.3% on launch of new foldable phone. Comcast -6.6%. FX: [USN:L4N45102E TEXT:"Dollar/yen"] hovers around 7-month low. BONDS: U.S., UK, European yields spike to multi-year highs. The highest U.S. 10-year yield in three years draws strong demand at 10-year auction — bid/cover highest in over a decade, according to Wrightson ICAP. COMMODITIES/METALS: [USN:P8N43I0BY TEXT:"Oil"] marches higher, Brent tops $100/bbl. U.S. diesel at record $5.94/gallon. Today's Talking Points: Our House "I am the house now," U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott [USN:L1N451007 TEXT:"Bessent"] said on Tuesday. "And you can bet against me if you want." Bessent's eye-opening remarks were in reference to his knowledge of, and influence over, the Japanese yen. Remember, the U.S. jointly intervened with Japan to support the yen a few weeks ago. Bessent's swagger here appears to be well-founded — for now at least — with the yen rallying strongly across the board. Of course, time will tell. But it's a different story in the U.S. bond market, where Bessent is even more active, trying to get longer-end yields down. Treasury on Wednesday said it will buy back up to [USN:L1N4510P7 TEXT:"$6 billion of long-dated bonds"] on Thursday, three times its last buyback. But yields leaped to new, historic highs on the announcement. The U.S. bond market is big, there are big bets being made. Again, time will tell. But the house may not always win here. High energy Brent crude oil is back above $100/bbl, WTI isn't far behind and is at a 3-month high. Oil is now up 50% on the same period a year ago. Meanwhile, U.S. gasoline prices are comfortably above $4/gallon, and diesel is at a record $5.94/gallon. War in the Middle East is spreading, and there's little to suggest peace, resolution or ceasefire are anywhere close on the horizon. Puzzling questions from all this are: [USN:L6N4500VT TEXT:"why isn't the economy rolling over"], and will it ever? Of course, the economy is much less energy-intensive now than it was in years gone by, and as we are seeing elsewhere, many traditional macro models, rules of thumb, and correlations have broken down since the COVID-19 pandemic. High energy costs are one of the factors lifting bond yields, and stocks may now be feeling the heat. Are the scales beginning to tip? The fold rush Apple shares have performed reasonably well this year, outperforming all of its "Magnificent 7" peers except Nvidia. Investors have cheered Apple's conservative approach to borrowing — it has eschewed the debt issuance binge many of its peers have undertaken to fund the AI buildout. Apple's market cap briefly topped $5 trillion in July, becoming only the second company to achieve that milestone after Nvidia. But doubts persist around new products and pricing. If the initial share price move on Wednesday following the launch of the company's [USN:L6N4510Z3 TEXT:"foldable phone called "Duo""] is any indication, these doubts aren't lifting any time soon. The cheapest Duo will be $1,999, and that's not cheap. Shares initially fell more than 2% on the unveiling, but recouped most of these losses to end down only 0.3%. That still lagged other Mag 7 and Big Tech stocks, however. What could move markets tomorrow? item.title: Fachin tira inquérito das fake news de Alexandre de Moraes
item.description: O presidente do Supremo Tribunal Federal, Edson Fachin, retirou o ministro Alexandre de Moraes da condução do chamado inquérito das fake news a partir desta quarta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente do Supremo Tribunal Federal, Edson Fachin, retirou o ministro Alexandre de Moraes da condução do chamado inquérito das fake news a partir desta quarta-feira. Instaurado em 2019, o inquérito visava investigar ataques ao STF e acabou ampliando as atribuições de Moraes. Em sua decisão, Fachin ressalta que todas as medidas tomadas até o momento são válidas. Outras investigações e procedimentos ainda em aberto serão enviados à presidência do STF.

item.title: AI models’ capabilities leap comes with new safety warnings
item.description: At Goldman Sachs’ annual tech investor gathering, Communacopia + Technology Conference, in San Francisco this week, who wasn’t in the room mattered almost as much as who was.
item.dc:creator: Krystal Hu
item.content:encoded: At Goldman Sachs’ annual tech investor gathering, Communacopia + Technology Conference, in San Francisco this week, who wasn’t in the room mattered almost as much as who was. Investors packed OpenAI CFO [USN:L6N450178 TEXT:"Sarah Friar’s session"], but in the hallways another question kept coming up: Where is Anthropic’s IPO S-1 filing? The company skipped its usual appearance as it prepares for what could be one of the largest IPOs ever. The filing would give investors their first detailed look at how Anthropic’s much-discussed annualized revenue translates into booked GAAP revenue, what its compute costs really look like, and whether private-market valuations can withstand public-market scrutiny. For now, they’ll have to wait a little longer, as the timeline has [USN:L6N44W17K TEXT:"slipped by a few weeks"]. As capital tries to decide just how long the AI boom can keep running, I’ve been trading notes with my colleague Deepa Seetharaman, who has been immersed in a very different corner of the AI world: researchers increasingly worried that the technology is advancing faster than humans can understand or control it. She has been breaking stories on the prime example of that tension — an OpenAI agent that went rogue long before the incident became public, and the company’s decision not to disclose it at the time. So this week, we’re looking at two sides of the same race: investors betting the boom can keep accelerating, and the people building the technology asking whether it should. Scroll on. OUR LATEST REPORTING IN TECH AND AI [USN:L6N45014G TEXT:"Apple shows off iPhone 18 Pro at start of event expected to debut folding phones"] [USN:L6N4510WC TEXT:"OpenAI’s rogue agents used at least 10 more sites for unauthorized comms, researchers say"] [USN:L4N4500M5 TEXT:"China's DeepSeek taps CITIC Securities for domestic IPO, sources say"] [USN:L4N4501G4 TEXT:"Suno releases new AI music models in partnership with Warner Music, BMG"] [USN:L8N44Z0XI TEXT:"Teen reading slumps to worst this century due to surge in screen time"] [USN:S0N4490CN TEXT:"US, China gear up for mid-September AI safety talks"] [USN:L6N44W0BR TEXT:"From dance floor to war: China readies humanoid robots for combat"] THE AI RACE NO ONE CAN AFFORD TO SLOW The past seven days captured the tension defining the AI world right now: frontier models are getting more capable, investors are rewarding the companies building them, yet some of the people closest to those models are getting increasingly alarmed about where the race is heading. Take OpenAI’s new Astra model launched last week. It represents a substantial jump over previous generations. OpenAI employees who are among Astra’s heaviest users burn roughly $7,000 worth of tokens a day, or about $1.5 million a year. Frontier models like Astra also helped train OpenAI’s lighter-weight ones; the company did an 80% price cut on one of those cheaper models and helped [USN:L6N450178 TEXT:"drive a tenfold"] increase in usage. Investors have noticed. Shares in SoftBank, one of OpenAI’s biggest financial backers, have jumped nearly 30% in the past five days as enthusiasm around its AI bets has grown. But as the money celebrates the capability gains, the same advances are setting off alarms elsewhere. Astra arrived amid growing scrutiny of how OpenAI trains and monitors increasingly capable agents. OpenAI’s own system card — the technical report outlining how it tested the model — showed a [USN:L6N44V0KT TEXT:"substantial deterioration"] in so-called monitorability, or researchers’ ability to understand what the model is doing internally. OpenAI said Astra is more likely than earlier models to intentionally conceal or disguise its step-by-step reasoning, making it harder for humans to evaluate how it reached an answer. On more complicated problems, the model is also getting better at covering its tracks. That is particularly uncomfortable given another controversy hanging over the company. Last week, [USN:L6N44W08B TEXT:"Reuters reported exclusively"] that OpenAI knew about a swarm of AI agents targeting a German wiki but did not publicly disclose the incident. A [USN:L6N4510WC TEXT:"follow-up investigation shows"] AI agents launched by OpenAI used at least 10 previously undisclosed websites for unsanctioned communications earlier this year. OpenAI said it did not disclose the case because it was similar to other incidents it had already made public. Taken together, the developments are unsettling some researchers who say capability gains are arriving faster than they expected, even as humans have less visibility into — and potentially less control over — how the models operate. The German wiki case raises a separate but related question: how much should the public trust the companies building these systems to police themselves when greater capability may come at the expense of monitorability? That concern is increasingly coming from inside the labs themselves. Even OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki has suggested that leading labs should be willing to coordinate a voluntary slowdown if needed to build confidence in their safety measures. Other OpenAI researchers have expressed similar ideas. Aidan Clark wrote that, for the first time, he was asking himself whether “things are moving too fast.” Boaz Barak said employees were beginning to feel “viscerally the magnitude of capabilities” and “there are also many ways it can end up very badly.” Anthropic has positioned itself as the more safety-conscious frontier lab, but is not immune to these concerns. This week, its researcher Jacob Coxon, who previously worked at OpenAI, resigned and accused both companies of racing toward self-improving superintelligence without acting responsibly. Some employees at both labs would like their leaders to reach an agreement on when and how to slow down. But that runs into a practical problem: there is [USN:L6N42D13P TEXT:"deep distrust "]between OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei. There is also an enormous amount of money riding on staying ahead. Anthropic is gearing up for the largest public listing in history that could value it at an astounding $2 trillion. OpenAI, meanwhile, needs financing to pay for the compute required to keep pushing its models forward. Every new capability can help justify the next funding round, infrastructure commitment or IPO. That leaves the frontier labs caught in several races at once: to build the most capable model, secure enough compute to train the next one, and reach the public markets before their rivals. The people actually building these systems are increasingly asking whether the pace itself has become a problem, and whether the trade-off between capability and control is becoming too dangerous. The harder question is whether anyone in the race can afford to be the first to slow down. CHART OF THE WEEK AI agents from OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta going rogue didn’t just alarm researchers. They also highlighted how quickly the cyber-risk landscape is changing for companies and insurers. Reported AI incidents have shifted sharply over the past decade: maliciously driven incidents now account for a much larger share of failures, while incidents tied primarily to system safety, failures and limitations have declined as a share of the total. As the industry is still learning what increasingly autonomous models can do, insurers are being asked to price risks that are evolving faster than the policy language designed to cover them. Insurers including MSIG and Beazley are taking notice, my colleagues [USN:L6N44A125 TEXT:"wrote"]. Insurance companies are reviewing traditional cyber policies and adjusting language to account for risks from more autonomous AI systems: agents that can escape controlled environments, take actions without direct human instruction and potentially carry out cyberattacks. That raises basic questions about whether an autonomous AI system fits traditional definitions of a cyber attacker and who is liable when an AI-generated action causes a loss.

item.title: 10-year yields highest since 2023
item.description: Benchmark 10-year Treasury yields reached their highest levels since 2023 on Wednesday after the announcement of an enlarged Treasury buyback of longer-dated bonds disappointed some investors who had wanted more.
item.dc:creator: Karen Brettell, Sinead Carew
item.content:encoded: Benchmark 10-year Treasury yields reached their highest levels since 2023 on Wednesday after the announcement of an enlarged Treasury buyback of longer-dated bonds disappointed some investors who had wanted more. Yields retreated from their highs, however, after the Treasury saw very strong demand for a $39 billion sale of 10-year notes. The [USN:L1N4510PH TEXT:"U.S. Treasury Department"] said it will buy up to $6 billion in 10- to 20-year Treasury bonds during its buyback operation on Thursday, triple the size of its last long-dated operation. "People thought the buyback was going to be larger than $6 billion. It was a disappointment so bond prices sank and yields rose," said Tom di Galoma, managing director at Mischler Financial. After a selloff that pushed 30-year yields to their highest level since 2007, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced in August that the government would increase buybacks of longer-dated bonds. Very strong demand for a 10-year note auction then brought yields off this highs, with the debt selling at the highest yield since 2007. "The auction came at a historical high for 2026 and buyers showed up with very strong demand. The reason they showed up in a very large way is because tomorrow the Treasury is going to buy 10-year to 20-year paper. Investors may have thought it was a risk-free trade," di Galoma said. Treasury Department sold the 10-year notes at a high yield of 4.834%, more than a basis point below where they traded ahead of the auction. Demand was 2.71 times the amount of debt on offer, the highest since 2019. The U.S. government already saw solid demand for its $58 billion sale of 3-year notes on Tuesday and will also sell $22 billion in 30-year bonds on Thursday. The yield on benchmark U.S. 10-year notes was last up 3.06 basis points at 4.835% after earlier reaching 4.8568%, the highest level since November 2023. The 30-year bond yield rose 2.06 basis points to 5.2846% after touching its highest level since August 18. The 2-year note yield, which typically moves in step with interest rate expectations for the Federal Reserve, rose 2.52 basis points to 4.423%, after earlier trading at 4.4316%, its highest level since July 2024. A closely watched part of the U.S. Treasury yield curve measuring the gap between yields on two- and 10-year Treasury notes, seen as an indicator of economic expectations, was at a positive 41.0 basis points. Meanwhile, oil prices breached $100 for the first time since July as the intensifying conflict in the Middle East heightened concerns about supply. The move came as investors waited for inflation data, which analysts say will be key to the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision next week. "The inflationary story is getting a little stickier, and that could cause the Fed to hike rates," said Lawrence Gillum, chief fixed income strategist for LPL Financial in Fort Mill, South Carolina. FED POLICYMAKERS MEET NEXT WEEK U.S. producer price and consumer price inflation reports are due to be released on Thursday and Friday, respectively. And analysts said the data will play a key role in whether the Fed hikes rates at its September 15-16 meeting. Rising oil prices have reignited concerns that higher fuel costs will flow through to consumer inflation and add to inflation that is already running above the U.S. central bank's 2% annual target. Traders raised bets on a rate hike at the Fed's meeting next week after the Labor Department reported on Friday that employers added [USN:L1N44W0EC TEXT:"far more positions"] than expected in August. Fed funds futures traders are now pricing in about 60% odds of a rate hike next week.

item.title: Gauff fights back to beat Andreeva and reach US Open semis
item.description: American Coco Gauff saved two match points to beat Russian fifth seed Mirra Andreeva 2-6 7-6(7) 6-2 on Wednesday and reach the U.S. Open semi-finals after recovering from a dreadful opening set.
item.dc:creator: Amy Tennery
item.content:encoded: American Coco Gauff saved two match points to beat Russian fifth seed Mirra Andreeva 2-6 7-6(7) 6-2 on Wednesday and reach the U.S. Open semi-finals after recovering from a dreadful opening set. The 2023 champion had none of her usual firepower at first and was on the ropes in the tiebreak before she flipped the script and closed out the match with a forehand strike, dropping her racket to the court in joy and relief. She faces second seed Elena Rybakina in the last four. Andreeva looked completely at home in Arthur Ashe Stadium as she sprinted through the first four games, never allowing Gauff to set up a break-point chance in the opening set where the Russian had just five unforced errors to 14 from her opponent. The two players settled into a fine fight in the second set, trading breaks twice before the tiebreak, where Gauff deployed a perfectly placed backhand to win a 39-shot rally and twice saved match point. Andreeva flung her racket at her bench in disgust after dropping her serve in the third game of the decider and Gauff broke her to love in the seventh game to put the contest completely out of reach.

item.title: Oklahoma judge used AI in ruling that contained false citations, prosecutor says
item.description: An Oklahoma judge has acknowledged that a ruling he issued contained fictitious citations generated by artificial intelligence, according to state records, adding to a growing number of cases in which judges have faced scrutiny over AI use.
item.dc:creator: Mike Scarcella
item.content:encoded: An Oklahoma judge has acknowledged that a ruling he issued contained fictitious citations generated by artificial intelligence, according to state records, adding to a growing number of cases in which judges have faced scrutiny over AI use. The judge, Lawrence Wheeler of the District Court of Stephens County, told an investigator with the Oklahoma State Bureau of Investigation that he used OpenAI’s ChatGPT for research, and that an order he drafted contained two citations to cases that do not exist, according to an August 17 letter from a prosecutor to the state attorney general's office. Wheeler, who was elected in 2022 and presides over a family law docket, did not immediately respond to a request for comment left with his office in Duncan, Oklahoma. His lawyer, Scott Anderson, said in a statement that “Judge Wheeler and I have no comment on the matter at this time.” Wheeler's use of AI was included in a judicial misconduct complaint that also alleged that the judge secretly listened to jury deliberations, county district attorney Jason Hicks said in the letter, which was reviewed by Reuters. The Oklahoman newspaper first reported the letter. The Oklahoma Attorney General’s Office in a statement on Wednesday said it reviewed the allegations but the evidence was insufficient to prosecute. The office said the Oklahoma Supreme Court and another state judicial body have power to discipline judges whether or not there is a criminal violation. The growing use of AI technology in the courts and at law firms has put new scrutiny on the accuracy of filings and orders, stemming from instances where AI has made up case citations or misquoted the law. Two federal judges last year said the use of AI in their chambers [USN:L1N3W40R4 TEXT:"led to errors"] in two court rulings. A Georgia [USN:L6N41I0SY TEXT:"prosecutor’s use of AI"] led to erroneous citations appearing in a ruling in a murder case. OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment. According to the August 17 letter, Hicks recused himself from investigating Wheeler and asked Oklahoma State Attorney General Gentner Drummond to review the Oklahoma State Bureau of Investigation's report or reassign the inquiry. Drummond’s office in its statement on Wednesday said its criminal division “thoroughly reviewed” the claims and was not pursuing them further. The Oklahoma Council on Judicial Complaints in a statement on Wednesday said it cannot comment on or confirm any investigation. The Oklahoma Supreme Court did not immediately respond to a request for comment. item.title: Want a leveraged ETF but short on time? This one lasts just an hour
item.description: If a trading day seems awfully long, one exchange-traded fund provider believes it has just the product for you.
item.dc:creator: Suzanne McGee
item.content:encoded: If a trading day seems awfully long, one exchange-traded fund provider believes it has just the product for you. Defiance ETFs is seeking to offer investors 16 funds that aim to double a stock's return in a single hour — the latest product of the industry's race to amplify the returns on individual stocks for those who obsess over every twist and turn in Magnificent 7 stocks and other hot investments. The new products would work the same way as existing 2x single-stock funds, but with a reset that happens at the end of every hour rather than at the end of a regular U.S. trading day, which runs from 9:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. ET. "They treat the trading day as a single hour instead of a full day," said Sylvia Jablonski, CEO and chief investment officer at Defiance. The funds, which would be tied to the underlying performance of some of the most widely held and traded stocks and ETFs, ranging from Nvidia (NVDA.O) and Microsoft (MSFT.O) to the Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM.Z) , give investors a way to bet on intraday movements. Defiance's U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission filing comes as regulators [USN:L6N44T14I TEXT:"review"] a category of funds that includes such leveraged vehicles. The number of leveraged ETFs aiming to deliver double the return on individual stocks over a single day [USN:L6N4480VM TEXT:"continues to multiply"]. If users roll any gains into successive hours, and the market continues to work in their favor, compounding could allow them to capture larger gains over a single day than they would from simply buying the existing leveraged ETFs, Jablonski added. If, however, the stock reverses course or follows a choppy path to a one-day gain, investors could end up with a loss if they hang on to these hourly products, Jablonski said. The proposed products, which could begin trading in November if regulators do not object, are another new frontier in leveraged ETFs. The [USN:L2N3VX0LA TEXT:"SEC has so far blocked"] proposed leveraged products [USN:L3N3VW1HH TEXT:"offering 3x or 5x"] the daily returns of an underlying stock. Retail investors have accounted for [USN:L6N3ZJ0WY TEXT:"most trading"] in leveraged ETFs, but in its SEC filing, Defiance said the proposed products are suitable only for knowledgeable investors who understand the risks and can monitor their portfolios throughout the day. The SEC did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the latest filing.

item.title: Vídeo da Times Square mostra torcida pelo Brasil na Copa, não protesto contra Moraes
item.description: Um vídeo de pessoas vestidas de verde e amarelo na Times Square, em Nova York, não mostra um protesto contra o ministro Alexandre de Moraes, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), como dizem posts no Instagram e no Threads. As imagens são da torcida brasileira durante a Copa do Mundo deste ano.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Um vídeo de pessoas vestidas de verde e amarelo na Times Square, em Nova York, não mostra um protesto contra o ministro Alexandre de Moraes, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), como dizem posts no Instagram e no Threads. As imagens são da torcida brasileira durante a Copa do Mundo deste ano. Aqui estão os principais detalhes: O vídeo foi publicado por um perfil no Instagram em 13 de junho deste ano, dia da partida entre Brasil e Marrocos pela Copa do Mundo. “Tivemos uma vista incrível da Times Square enquanto nossos amigos brasileiros comemoravam a Copa do Mundo em Nova York”, escreveu a usuária. O site Metrópoles replicou as imagens em seu perfil no TikTok e entrevistou a autora, que contou ser norte-americana e disse que estava passeando pela Times Square no dia do jogo. À época, a imprensa noticiou que a torcida brasileira estava reunida na Times Square para assistir à partida. O cenário que aparece na filmagem corresponde à área da 7ª Avenida em frente à loja de roupas American Eagle, como mostram registros do Google Street View . Na última segunda-feira, Moraes foi alvo de manifestações em diversas capitais do Brasil após a revelação de conversas entre o ministro e o ex-dono do Banco Master, Daniel Vorcaro, investigado por fraudes financeiras bilionárias. A Reuters não localizou registros de protestos recentes contra Moraes em Nova York. Veredicto: Legenda errada. Um vídeo da torcida brasileira na Times Square durante a Copa do Mundo foi atribuído a um suposto protesto contra Moraes no local.

item.title: Fachin cassa decisões liminares de Mendonça e Dino sobre diretor-geral da PF, que segue no cargo por ora
item.description: O presidente do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), Edson Fachin, cassou as decisões liminares concedidas anteriormente pelos colegas André Mendonça e Flávio Dino que discutiam a permanência ou não do diretor-geral da Polícia Federal, Andrei Rodrigues, no cargo, segundo decisão tornada pública na tarde desta quarta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), Edson Fachin, cassou as decisões liminares concedidas anteriormente pelos colegas André Mendonça e Flávio Dino que discutiam a permanência ou não do diretor-geral da Polícia Federal, Andrei Rodrigues, no cargo, segundo decisão tornada pública na tarde desta quarta-feira. Fachin informou na decisão que Andrei Rodrigues vai permanecer no cargo por ora até uma nova decisão da própria presidência do STF. Ele deu 48 horas para que o chefe da PF preste informações no caso. Em nota, a Advocacia-Geral da União, que havia recorrido a Fachin, comemorou a decisão. "A decisão restaura a ordem pública e administrativa e, sobretudo, reafirma a prerrogativa constitucional privativa do presidente da República para prover e desprover os cargos de direção da Polícia Federal", destacou.

item.title: Angel Yin feeling fit for Solheim Cup: 'Would never jeopardize America'
item.description: Angel Yin said she is "feeling great" and ready to represent the United States in the Solheim Cup this weekend.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Angel Yin said she is "feeling great" and ready to represent the United States in the Solheim Cup this weekend. "I would never jeopardize America," Yin told reporters on Wednesday at Bernardus Golf in Cromvoirt, Netherlands. Yin, 27, lost 35 pounds this summer while battling a stomach illness. She returned to the LPGA Tour for the FM Championship at TPC Boston late last month, missing the cut with rounds of 81 and 76 and leading to speculation about her fitness for the Solheim Cup. "It wasn't ideal. It's not a score you really bring out and you go, wow, that's the person that's going to be -- you know, helping America bring home the Cup," Yin said of her performance in Boston. "I've been working hard, I've been trying everything I can, because this is the biggest event in women's golf and to be able to do it in this scale -- we know this is going to be a big deal because this is the 20th Solheim Cup." The U.S. team brought along an alternate, former World No. 1 Lilia Vu, for the biennial competition against Team Europe that begins on Friday. Yin, who had to withdraw from the KPMG Women's PGA Championship in late June, has three top-10 finishes on the LPGA Tour this season but none since a T9 at the Mizuho Americas Open from May 7-10. She was asked about the state of her game on Wednesday. "I guess everybody has different opinions," Yin said. "I personally think it's not bad. Every day it's getting better. So, yeah, I guess it's like art, right? Everybody has a different opinion. But results just is the only thing that matters, right? Yin said she felt ready to go in whatever role Team USA captain Angela Stanford chooses. "So I had, like, honest talks with myself in the mirror and with my team, and obviously with Angela because she's the only other person, other than my family, that I've updated throughout all of this," Yin said. "So, you know, I think that we are pretty -- we have a clear idea of what it is, and so, yeah, we all agreed on this. And she wanted me here. Because we asked her -- well, I didn't ask her. I had my caddie ask her, Do you want me here? And if she said no, I wouldn't be here. But she said yes. "So I think with belief like that and confidence from her to back me, why wouldn't I show up? The end." That wasn't the end of the conversation, however, as reporters asked several follow-up questions about how much she can contribute this weekend. "It's a tough decision because you don't want to jeopardize the team. I can say and be confident as much as I want, but ultimately it's up to the captain because she needs to be responsible for the 11 of us. Well, more because, you know, there's a whole country behind her. But I guess it's just more tough for her and I just need to do my part," Yin said. "And then I just need to wait for her call, and whatever she does and whatever she says will, in my opinion, be the best decision because we trust her, and she's been leading us great." --Field Level Media

item.title: Zheng’s unlikely New York run signals return to form
item.description: From the qualifying courts to the quarter-final stage, Zheng Qinwen exited the U.S. Open on Wednesday having sparked a career comeback, enjoying a return to form in a run few expected in New York.
item.dc:creator: Amy Tennery
item.content:encoded: From the qualifying courts to the quarter-final stage, Zheng Qinwen exited the U.S. Open on Wednesday having sparked a career comeback, enjoying a return to form in a run few expected in New York. The Olympic champion rode a rollercoaster of career ups and downs over the last two years, slipping from the top 10 in 2024 to 121st in the world after an elbow injury that threatened to [USN:L6N44Z0VQ TEXT:"completely derail"] her career. But an uninspiring 2026 campaign riddled with early exits gave way to one of the more compelling stories of the year's final major, where she became the first qualifier since Emma Raducanu in 2021 to reach the last eight. "The good thing is I know how to compete better than before than the beginning of the year," said Zheng, who lost on Wednesday to second seed Elena Rybakina 3-6 6-1 6-4. "In the beginning of the year, I was a bit totally out of tournament, like, rhythm, and obviously this tournament helps me to find myself little by little." Zheng became the tournament's ultimate escape artist, coming back from a five-game deficit in the deciding set against third-round foe Madison Keys and again in the opening set of her fourth-round match against six-times major winner Iga Swiatek. She can expect a hero's welcome at home with the Asia swing coming up on the calendar as one of China's brightest tennis stars. "I always am so excited to play in China, and especially coming from qualifying (for the) U.S. Open and then reaching until here. That was a really, really difficult journey for me," she told reporters. "I just want to keep calm and just train day by day, focus match by match, focus on the present, because when your mind is trying to go everywhere, thinking too much, that's not helping."

item.title: Foldable iPhone, pricier 18 Pro unveiled in Apple's first event under Ternus
item.description: Apple on Wednesday revealed its first foldable smartphone, iPhone Duo, and iPhone 18 Pro line-up in an event packed with device upgrades, offering a glimpse into how new CEO John Ternus intends to shape the company in the AI age.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Apple (AAPL.O) on Wednesday revealed its [USN:L1N4510JD TEXT:"first foldable smartphone"], iPhone Duo, and iPhone 18 Pro line-up in an event packed with device upgrades, offering a glimpse into how new CEO John Ternus intends to shape the company in the AI age. Here are the main takeaways from the event: DUO, APPLE'S BOLD NEW BET Duo marked the biggest redesign of the iPhone line in years. The passport-shaped device opens into a 7.6-inch display and features a 5.4-inch outer screen. The large display allows users to keep two apps open at the same time. The device is powered by Apple's A20 Pro chip, built on a 2-nanometer process. Apple said the chip, paired with a vapor-chamber cooling system, is designed to improve on-device AI performance, graphics processing and battery efficiency. Duo also includes Apple's latest C2 modem. Duo supports Apple Pencil and uses Touch ID integrated into the side button. Apple said it is the thinnest iPhone when open. Pricing starts at $1,999, about $100 more than Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold8 and Google's Pixel 11 Pro Fold at comparable base storage levels. Duo offers up to 2 terabytes of storage, a capacity not available on the rival foldable models. Pre-orders begin October 16 and the device goes on sale October 23. PRO MODELS GET COSTLIER WITH NEW 18 SERIES Apple gave its Pro Models a $100 price bump, with the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max starting at $1,199 and $1,299, increases forced by a surge in memory chip costs. Both the models are powered by Apple's new A20 Pro chip. They feature a new 48-megapixel main camera with a variable aperture system that automatically adjusts to lighting conditions and allows users greater control over depth of field and low-light photography. Apple also introduced Apple Reference Image, a photo-authentication standard and added support for SynthID to identify AI-generated or edited images. These feature will not be available in the European Union or China. APPLE INTELLIGENCE'S PRIVACY FOCUS Ternus, in his first Apple event as CEO, framed privacy as Apple's key differentiator in the AI era. He pitched the iPhone as an "intelligent personal hub" that ran AI services on-device whenever possible, with Siri playing a key role. The Cupertino, California-based company said cloud-based processing is used only when additional computing power is required, with privacy protections extended through its Private Cloud Compute system. Siri AI, meanwhile, will work with more than 300,000 apps at launch and can perform actions across Apple and third-party applications. APPLE WATCH The company launched the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4, featuring a redesigned health-sensing system and new S11 chip. Series 12 starts at $399, while Ultra 4 starts at $799. New features include a Readiness score, more frequent heart-rate monitoring, health insights powered by Apple Intelligence and new audio intelligence tools such as Live Rewind and Siri Recap. AIRPODS Apple launched a new generation of AirPods starting at $129, bringing active noise cancellation to its entry-level earbuds for the first time. A $149 version adds wireless charging and on-stem volume controls, allowing users to adjust volume by swiping up or down on the stem.

item.title: Braves put RHP Bryce Elder (knee) on IL, activate RHP Reynaldo Lopez
item.description: The Atlanta Braves placed Bryce Elder on the 15-day injured list following right knee surgery and activated fellow righty Reynaldo Lopez from the list on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Atlanta Braves placed Bryce Elder on the 15-day injured list following right knee surgery and activated fellow righty Reynaldo Lopez from the list on Wednesday. Elder's move was retroactive to Sunday. He had bone fragments removed from his right knee on Monday after feeling discomfort since the All-Star break. The 27-year-old last pitched on Aug. 31, allowing five runs on eight hits and three walks with three strikeouts in 5 1/3 innings in a 7-3 home loss to the San Francisco Giants. "He flew from (Philadelphia to Dallas) to get his knee checked out because it hasn't been getting better," Braves manager Walt Weiss said on Tuesday. "We've been giving him extended rest. He's been dealing with it since the All-Star break. It felt like the best chance for him to be a factor in the postseason is if he got this thing fixed." Weiss said Elder possibly could return following the end of the regular season on Sept. 27. "This was the only way (Elder coming back in the postseason) was going to happen, is if he had the surgery immediately to give him enough time to possibly make that happen," Weiss said. Elder is 8-8 with a 4.11 ERA, 49 walks and 121 strikeouts in 149 innings over 26 starts this season. For his career, Elder is 32-32 with a 4.46 ERA, 203 walks and 473 strikeouts in 583 2/3 innings over 105 regular-season games (104 starts) since 2022. He was an All-Star in 2023. Atlanta selected Elder in the fifth round of the 2020 MLB Draft out of the University of Texas. Lopez, 32, last pitched on July 26, posting 5 2/3 scoreless innings with one walk and six strikeouts in the Braves' 3-2 win in 11 innings at Baltimore. He went on the injured list with left knee inflammation on Aug. 2, retroactive to July 30. Lopez is 4-3 with a 3.64 ERA, 29 walks and 66 strikeouts in 71 2/3 innings over 24 games (11 starts). He has a career record of 51-57 with six saves, a 3.91 ERA, 322 walks and 832 strikeouts in 892 innings over 292 regular-season games (134 starts) with the Washington Nationals (2016), Chicago White Sox (2017-23), Los Angeles Angels (2023), Cleveland Guardians (2023) and Braves (2024-present). Lopez was an All-Star for Atlanta in the 2024 season. In other moves on Wednesday, the Braves selected the contract of left-hander Bailey Falter from Triple-A Gwinnett and activated him, and designated right-hander Elieser Hernandez for assignment. The Braves obtained Falter, 29, and outfielder Lane Thomas from the Kansas City Royals on Aug. 2 for two minor league pitchers. Falter was 0-2 in five games (two starts) for the Royals this season with six walks and six strikeouts in 9 2/3 innings. He was 2-0 with a 0.00 ERA, two walks and 11 strikeouts in 10 2/3 innings for Gwinnett. Hernandez, 31, was 2-0 with one save, a 2.45 ERA, six walks and 11 strikeouts in 11 innings over four relief appearances this season for Atlanta. He was 2-5 with a 4.54 ERA, 27 walks and 76 strikeouts in 81 1/3 innings in 23 games (11 starts) for Gwinnett. --Field Level Media

item.title: Oposición venezolana perderá pronto la supervisión del refinador Citgo: fuentes.
item.description: Juntas lideradas por la oposición venezolana que han supervisado al refinador estadounidense Citgo Petroleum durante los últimos siete años se preparan para cesar sus funciones —posiblemente este mismo mes— tras una reestructuración impulsada por la presidenta encargada de Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, según informaron dos fuentes vinculadas a los preparativos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Juntas lideradas por la oposición venezolana que han supervisado al refinador estadounidense Citgo Petroleum durante los últimos siete años se preparan para cesar sus funciones —posiblemente este mismo mes— tras una reestructuración impulsada por la presidenta encargada de Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, según informaron dos fuentes vinculadas a los preparativos. A principios de este año, Rodríguez inició los preparativos para recuperar el control del refinador, propiedad de Venezuela, después de que Washington reconociera formalmente a su gobierno, el cual sustituyó a la administración de Nicolás Maduro tras la captura de este último por parte de Estados Unidos en enero. Desde entonces, la administración de la presidenta encargada ha cambiado los bufetes de abogados que representaban a Venezuela y a la estatal petrolera PDVSA en litigios y arbitrajes en el extranjero, sustituyendo a los contratados por la Asamblea Nacional liderada por la oposición, según documentos judiciales estadounidenses. "Las junta directivas ya no son reconocidas como válidas por todas las contrapartes políticas y legales, por lo que no pueden continuar", señaló una de las fuentes. "Lamentablemente, esto está ocurriendo sin ninguna discusión previa". El Ministerio de Hidrocarburos de Venezuela, PDVSA, Citgo y las juntas supervisoras no respondieron de inmediato a las solicitudes de comentarios.

item.title: Navan raises fiscal 2027 forecast on strong corporate travel demand, customer growth
item.description: Navan raised its full-year forecasts for revenue and operating income on Wednesday, as strong demand for business travel and addition of new customers drive growth.
item.dc:creator: Shivansh Tiwary
item.content:encoded: Navan (NAVN.O) raised its full-year forecasts for revenue and operating income on Wednesday, as strong demand for business travel and addition of new customers drive growth. However, shares of the corporate travel and expense platform fell 13% after the bell. Business travel has remained resilient despite geopolitical uncertainty, with corporate investment in artificial intelligence prompting sales teams, engineers and executives to travel more frequently. A fuller calendar of industrials conferences and an increase in cross-border dealmaking have also supported corporate booking volumes. Navan, which went public in October last year, said gross booking volume grew 45% in its second quarter, while payment volume grew 34%. "Demand for corporate travel has been very, very strong," CFO Aurélien Nolf told Reuters in an interview. "On average, every traveler is (taking) more trips year over year. And each of those trips is on average generating higher bookings than they were a year ago." Navan now expects revenue of $927 million to $933 million for the fiscal year ending January 31, 2027, up from its prior forecast of $907 million to $913 million. It forecast adjusted operating income in the range of $82 million to $86 million, compared with its earlier expectations of $76 million to $80 million Separately, Navan said it would acquire AI-powered event-management platform BoomPop for an undisclosed amount. The deal was valued at up to $95 million in cash and stock, according to a person familiar with the matter. Navan forecast third-quarter revenue in the range of $253 million to $255 million, compared with analysts' expectations of $248.27 million, according to data compiled by LSEG. For the second quarter, the company reported an adjusted profit per share of 5 cents, compared with 4 cents expected by the Wall Street. Revenues for the same period rose 35% to $233 million, beating analysts' expectations of $220.46 million.

item.title: Venezuela's opposition to soon lose Citgo oversight, sources say
item.description: The Venezuelan opposition-controlled boards that have supervised U.S. refiner Citgo Petroleum during the last seven years are preparing to wind down as soon as this month following a shake-up by Venezuelan interim President Delcy Rodriguez, two sources involved in the preparations said.
item.dc:creator: Marianna Parraga
item.content:encoded: The Venezuelan opposition-controlled boards that have supervised U.S. refiner Citgo Petroleum during the last seven years are preparing to wind down as soon as this month following a shake-up by Venezuelan interim President Delcy Rodriguez, two sources involved in the preparations said. Rodriguez earlier this year began preparations to [USN:L1N40I0RL TEXT:"regain control"] of the Venezuela-owned refiner after her government, which replaced Nicolas Maduro's administration after he was captured by the U.S. in January, was recognized formally by Washington. The interim President's administration has since [USN:L1N42J0ZT TEXT:"swapped"] law firms that had represented Venezuela and state-run oil company PDVSA in lawsuits and arbitration cases abroad, replacing the ones hired by an opposition-led National Assembly, according to U.S. court filings. "The boards are no longer recognized as valid by all political and legal counterparties, so they can no longer continue," one of the sources said. "This is happening, unfortunately, without any previous discussion." Venezuela's oil ministry, PDVSA, Citgo and the supervising boards did not immediately reply to requests for comment.

item.title: American Eagle sticks to annual sales forecast amid cautious spending
item.description: American Eagle Outfitters reiterated its annual comparable sales forecast on Wednesday, as consumers pulled back on spending on discretionary items including apparel.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: American Eagle Outfitters (AEO.N) reiterated its annual comparable sales forecast on Wednesday, as consumers pulled back on spending on discretionary items including apparel. Shares fell about 10% in extended trading. Demand for apparel has remained uneven as inflationary pressures and macroeconomic uncertainty prompt shoppers to focus on essentials such as gas and groceries and wait for promotions before buying clothing and accessories. American Eagle, like peers such as Gap, has been navigating challenges including weakness in certain seasonal categories in the last few months. American Eagle posted quarterly revenue of $1.38 billion, above analysts' estimates of $1.37 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG. The company reiterated its annual comparable sales forecast for the second time and raised its operating income target after including the impact of $196 million in tariff refunds received during the second quarter. American Eagle still expects fiscal 2026 comparable sales to be up mid-single-digits. It sees operating income in the range of $540 million to $550 million, compared with a prior range of $390 million to $410 million.

item.title: Fafá de Belém fez show contra dosimetria em 2025, não em apoio a Lula em 2026
item.description: Um show da cantora Fafá de Belém em frente a uma multidão com bandeiras do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva e do PT na praia de Copacabana, no Rio de Janeiro, ocorreu em dezembro do ano passado, quando a artista se apresentou em um protesto contra a proposta de dosimetria para condenados por ataques antidemocráticos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Um show da cantora Fafá de Belém em frente a uma multidão com bandeiras do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva e do PT na praia de Copacabana, no Rio de Janeiro, ocorreu em dezembro do ano passado, quando a artista se apresentou em um protesto contra a proposta de dosimetria para condenados por ataques antidemocráticos. Nas redes sociais, porém, posts compartilham o registro como se mostrasse uma manifestação da cantora em apoio a Lula no 7 de Setembro deste ano. Aqui estão os principais detalhes: “Nesse 7 de Setembro, Fafá de Belém arrasta multidões em show do PT”, alega a legenda de uma postagem no Instagram . Nas imagens, a cantora se apresenta em frente ao Posto 5 e usa uma camiseta branca. Os perfis no Instagram de Fafá e da Mídia Ninja compartilharam o mesmo vídeo em 14 de dezembro de 2025, que mostra com mais nitidez a estampa da camiseta da cantora. “ Ato Musical 2: o retorno. Rio de Janeiro nas ruas ”, diz. O evento reuniu diversos artistas em protesto contra o projeto da dosimetria , que reduzia as penas de condenados pelos ataques relacionados à tentativa de golpe de Estado após as eleições de 2022. O Congresso Nacional aprovou a proposta em dezembro do ano passado, mas Lula a vetou integralmente no mês seguinte. Já em abril, os parlamentares derrubaram o veto de Lula. O ministro Alexandre de Moraes suspendeu em maio a aplicação da lei até que o Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) analise sua constitucionalidade. A assessoria de imprensa de Fafá confirmou à Reuters que o vídeo é antigo e disse que a cantora está em Portugal desde o início de setembro. Neste 7 de Setembro, o candidato a presidente Augusto Cury (Avante) promoveu uma passeata entre os Postos 5 e 6 da praia de Copacabana -- mesmo local do registro checado. Além disso, o Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) proíbe os chamados showmícios para promover candidatos durante a campanha. Veredicto: Legenda errada. Fafá de Belém se apresentou na praia de Copacabana em dezembro de 2025 em protesto contra a dosimetria, e não em evento pró-Lula no 7 de Setembro deste ano.
